fit.sheet: RCA 2N404, 2N404A, 2N581, 2N582 data sheet (File No. 15, 9-66; RCA SPD-100 Semiconductor Products Databook, 1969)
fit.figure: page 2 table (typical hFE, VCE(sat), VBE(sat), ICBO, IEBO, fhfb, Cob); Fig. 2 minimum hFE, its shape to 30 mA; Figs. 3 and 4 minimum and maximum collector characteristics, their geometric middle's shape
fit.method: .claude/skills/fit-model/worked/germanium/alloy.py: the table's typicals (x3 weight) with the shape of the middle of Figs. 3/4 (up to a free factor, 0.799), at the sheet's own VCE (0.15-0.68 V), leakage included; IS, NF, BF, ISE, NE, IKF, NKF, RE, BR, ISC, NC, RC free, NR = NF. Below the table's 12 mA the leakage-free gain is held flat (0.5 to 12 mA, its level free): the sheet's one lower figure, Fig. 2, contradicts the table (see the note). No rbb' on the sheet, so RB 0; no output curves above 0.7 V, so no VAF. CJC from Cob 12 pF at 6 V (one point), TF from fhfb 13 MHz taken as fT. Fitted points within 5.3 % (hFE), 11.2 mV (VCE(sat)) and 16.5 mV (VBE(sat)) of the table; ICBO 1.40 µA, IEBO 1.41 µA. Curves read off the raster by pixel (.claude/skills/fit-model/worked/germanium/pix.py)
fit.note: Our own fit by pixel from RCA's sheet. The sheet has no typical curves: the card is its table's typicals (12 and 24 mA, near saturation) with the shape of the middle of its minimum and maximum curves to 110 mA. Nothing on the sheet goes below 12 mA that agrees with the table (Fig. 2 contradicts it), so the gain is held flat below 12 mA: at a pedal's 0.3-2 mA, and on the tester, the figure is the card's extrapolation. Germanium units vary widely (hFE 30 min at 12 mA, no max): give a measured hFE and leakage (D-130).
